4Halloran Meadows

Most people turn around at Echo Point. Keep climbing and you come out on a wide bench of meadow at 6,230 feet. Wildflowers peak in July, and it's the best place in the park to see elk.

Status
Open
Distance
6.4 mi
Climb
2,690 ft
Time
5 hr
Start
Basin Lodge trailhead, by way of Echo Point
Terrain
Steep to Echo Point, then a long run of switchbacks. Level across the meadows.

The trail starts at the Basin Lodge trailhead and climbs steeply through the trees to the rail at Echo Point. That first half mile is the hardest part of the day, so catch your breath at the top and give the cliffs a yell.

Past the point the trail heads uphill again and switchbacks a long way through the trees. It's easier going than the first half mile, but you don't get much of a view until the meadows.

You come out of the trees onto the meadows and the trail levels off across the bench. Halloran Creek runs through the middle and falls off the lower edge of the bench, above the head of the lake.

What to look for

Wildflowers
They peak in July. Please keep to the trail through them, because a shortcut kills plants that take twenty years to grow back.
Elk
A herd of about sixty grazes here most evenings. Bring binoculars and stay at least 25 yards back.
The view
It's the only place in the park where you can see the lake and the pass at the same time. Walk down to the lower edge of the meadow for the best of it.

Before you go

  • Allow five hours, and longer if you're staying for the elk. If you are, you'll be walking down after sunset, so bring a headlamp.
  • Bring water and a warm layer. There's no cell coverage past the lodge.
